questions.question: Why is thumbs-down rate a weak production metric on its own?
options: Few users rate (about 6–7% here), and unhappy users rate more, so it's sparse and biased
questions.explanation: Both versions showed 55% thumbs-down while v2 was clearly worse on escalations.

questions.question: Which signal revealed v2's problem across every conversation?
questions.explanation: Implicit signals cover all conversations, not just the few that get rated.

questions.question: Why does canary_check require both a minimum effect and p < 0.01?
options: Effect size alone alarms on noise; significance alone alarms on differences too small to matter at high traffic
To make alerts rarer for no reason
questions.explanation: You want differences that are both real and big enough to act on.

questions.question: The 10% canary never alerted, though v2 was truly worse. What does that mean?
options: The canary was too small to detect a 3.5-point difference in 5 days; silence is not evidence of safety
questions.explanation: At 30% traffic the same problem alerted on the second day.

questions.question: How should a human review queue be built?
options: Flagged conversations from the new version first, plus a random slice of unrated ones
questions.explanation: Most failures are never rated, so unrated samples catch what feedback misses.

questions.question: Before rolling out a new agent version, what should you decide first?
options: The smallest regression you must catch and how fast, then size the canary and duration to match
questions.explanation: Detection limits come from traffic and time; plan them deliberately.
